long_biography.plain_text:
IndusInd Bank was Srichand Hinduja's clearest individual institution-building project. He conceived it as a new-generation private bank, mobilised capital from the Indian diaspora and saw it open in 1994. Its name linked a modern financial venture to the trading culture of the Indus Valley.

That achievement sat within a larger family transformation. After their father died in 1971, Srichand and his brothers took charge of an Indo-Iranian trading business, shifted the group base to London and diversified through major acquisitions. Srichand led the purchases of Ashok Leyland and Gulf Oil, helping turn an inherited trading platform into a multinational conglomerate.
